children: Zillow reported higher third-quarter revenue as its rentals business helped it offset what it called "one of the toughest housing markets in a generation."
The company posted a loss of $158 million, or 70 cents a share, compared with a profit of $10 million, or 4 cents a share, the year prior.
Adjusted earnings were 55 cents a share. Analysts polled by FactSet expected 58 cents a share.
Revenue rose 7% to $724 million. Wall Street expected $753.7 million. Rentals revenue rose 26% to $220 million.
